maria.g: Heads-up — GitOps canary for the EU clusters failed during post-install hooks, noticed in the afternoon batch.
henry.s: saw that, got a couple of alarms. Which hook?
maria.g: the cni post-install job — it errored applying a new NetworkPolicy/egress annotation. Argo shows job stuck and then timed out.
ops-bot: CI/CD pipeline failed: job=github-actions/gitops-deploy, status=failed, exit_code=1
raj: paste of pod logs: ```Error: failed post-install: hook "cni-post-install" failed: Job failed: exit status 1
E0412 15:22:18.123456 1 networkpolicy_controller.go:42] unknown field "egressPolicy" in CNI config
```
alice.k: That unknown field was introduced by the helm chart v2.7.0 -> we added a top-level egressPolicy: "all" which the CNI operator rejects on k8s 1.24 in eu-west1 clusters.
maria.g: right — EU clusters are still on 1.24 for kernel compatibility, whereas canary target assumed 1.25. ArgoCD tried to apply and the CNI hook failed.
henry.s: Meanwhile cluster-autoscaler in eu-west1 started spamming scale events because the post-install job pinned PVs and schedulable nodes dropped. Logs: "scaleUp failed: insufficient capacity for pods with GPU=1"
raj: we're seeing spot evictions spike in that region today; AZ A has almost no spare GPUs, spot interruption rate up.
alice.k: If we force new on-demand nodegroup for the canary it'll succeed but cost goes up — roughly 3x for the burst window. Is that acceptable?
maria.g: ops wants minimal cost impact, but we also can't leave canary half-applied. Proposal: abort canary, rollback Argo app to previous commit and re-run after CNI chart fix.
infra-bot: Runbook snippet: rollback via argocd CLI: ```argocd app rollback infra-cni eu-canary-rollback --revision v2.6.3```
henry.s: +1 for rollback. Also we should pin chart to v2.6.3 for clusters <1.25 until we schedule kube upgrades.
raj: quick note — terraform apply for eu nodegroup (reserved-gpu-eu) is blocked by a remote state lock on the state bucket, someone left a workspace active. Error: "Error: state snapshot failed: state lock is held by session <id>"
maria.g: I see that, I freed the lock (saw a stale session) — re-running plan now.
alice.k: After rollback, let's patch the PR to the chart that conditionally emits egressPolicy only for k8s >=1.25. Simple if/else in the helm template.
raj: snippet suggestion: ```{{- if semverCompare ">=1.25.0" .Capabilities.KubeVersion.GitVersion }} egressPolicy: "all" {{- end }}```
henry.s: Also add a preflight ArgoCD hook to validate CRDs and CNI config on target cluster version before attempting post-install jobs. Saves us from half-applied state.
maria.g: agreed. I'll abort the current canary rollout and kick off rollback now.
ops-bot: user maria.g triggered: argocd app rollback infra-cni eu-canary-rollback — success
infra-bot: alert cleared: canary failed -> rolled back; recommend follow-ups: (1) chart guardrails, (2) kube version gating in gitops pipeline, (3) capacity check before canary.
alice.k: I'll open a PR for a conditional template + unit tests for chart rendering against kube 1.24 and 1.25.
raj: Action item for infra team: add a cheap capacity pre-check job in GitHub Actions that queries ASG/GKE node pools for GPU spare capacity in target region before applying canary. Command example: ```gcloud compute instance-templates list --filter="labels.cluster:eu"```
henry.s: We should also surface estimated incremental cost if fallback to on-demand is used. Quick calc: 10 nodes * $3.2/hr -> +$768/day. Put that in the rollback ticket so finance isn't surprised.
maria.g: adding notes to the incident ticket. Thanks everyone, will follow up once PR and pipeline guard are in place.
henry.s: one more: tag the rollback commit with "canary-rollback/eu-<ts>" for audit.
alice.k: done after PR: will add changelog entry and test matrix update.
ops-bot: incident ticket updated: #INC-4721 — status=rolling-back -> resolved-pending-followup
maria.g: closing thread once follow-ups are tracked. Thanks!
